data.narrative:
Humans& is an AI & Software company at an undisclosed stage with founders Eric Zelikman, Georges Harik, Noah Goodman, Andi Peng, and Yuchen He. The broader AI & Software sector includes 12 identifiable peers, of which 1 is public (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and 8 are private. Top private comparables include Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. Despite 12 same-sector companies existing, zero meet the narrow filtering criteria of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier simultaneously. Applying an all-sector median would introduce substantial bias given the heterogeneity of AI & Software business models, stage distributions, and capital structures. This screening failure reflects the difficulty of establishing reliable comps for frontier-stage AI companies where stage definitions, revenue models, and funding patterns diverge significantly.

Without sufficient narrow-set triangulation, a credible valuation range cannot be derived from the available data. Any estimate would require either additional stage clarity on Humans&, deeper financial metrics from private peers, or acceptance of wider confidence intervals inherent to early-stage AI valuations. The single public comp (Palantir) operates at a different maturity level and does not resolve the sparse-comparable problem. Further due diligence on deal-stage, revenue, and peer-stage alignment is necessary before triangulation can proceed.
